subject: Exec Roundtable - Boston: card pre-auth declined for a subset of attendees
messages:
From: Paul Ng <paul.ng@eventlogistics.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sarah.hartwell@hartwellpharma.com
Date: 2026-10-06T15:02:00-04:00
Subject: Pre-auth declines at Hotel Seaport — need backup plan

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Quick heads-up from the hotel billing team: the group pre-authorizations for three of the VIP rooms came back as declined this morning (AMEX flagged the corporate cards) when they attempted a pre-check-in hold. We’ve attached the merchant decline notice they provided.

Immediate implications:
- Rooms are being held but not yet guaranteed — hotel will hold rooms for 48 hours with a credit-card hold after which they release.
- Onsite incidentals and A/V vendor require a credit card on file; without that they are asking for either a deposit wire or card-on-file per attendee.

Options I can facilitate: process individual credit-card authorizations onsite (card present), accept AMEX prepayment link (they can provide), or we can receive a manual wire from Redwoods / client. The quickest workaround is to take payment by card at check-in or use a temporary corporate prepay card.

Please advise how you want us to proceed; Sarah from Hartwell is looping procurement on their side to see if they can temporarily cover the hold.

Attachments: AMEX_decline_notice.pdf (merchant notice)

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Ng
Event Logistics Manager | Beacon Events (vendor)
Office: 617-555-0198

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Paul Ng <paul.ng@eventlogistics.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: sarah.hartwell@hartwellpharma.com
Date: 2026-10-06T17:24:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Pre-auth declines at Hotel Seaport — need backup plan

Thanks Paul — and Sarah, appreciate the quick flag.

Short version: we need a temporary card/credit solution before the next check-in window (48 hours). Three attendees' corporate Amex authorizations failed: two C-suite and one external consultant. I don’t want us asking the C-suite to do a manual card present unless absolutely necessary.

Marissa / Rishi — can Finance push a one-time virtual card or prepay for the rooms and incidentals? If not, we’ll need a reimbursement path for any personal-card charges with same-day processing.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: confirm whether Redwood can issue a virtual card for Beacon Events (single-use) and cap to vendor charges only.
- Rishi: if virtual card not possible, please confirm expedited reimbursement (we’ll collect personal receipts) and who signs off.
- Paul: hold rooms for 48 hours and proceed with fallback (hotel will accept AMEX prepayment link — please send the link if we go that route).

I’ve attached the final onsite itinerary for reference.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-1290

From: AMEX Merchant Services <amex-support@amex.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, paul.ng@eventlogistics.com
Date: 2026-10-07T09:01:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Merchant decline reference 4512-10 (hotel pre-auth)

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 09:01 AM AMEX Merchant Services <amex-support@amex.com> wrote:

Hello team,

Per our investigation, the declines are due to new account-level card-holder verification flags AMEX rolled out for certain corporate BIN ranges for hotel pre-authorizations. The card authorizations themselves are not fraudulent; they tripped a higher-friction check (MOTO/Pre-auth channel mismatch).

We can temporarily whitelist Redwood’s merchant token for the Seaport property for a 72-hour window if you provide:
- Merchant token / hotel MID (we already have the merchant details from Beacon)
- A signed authorization from Redwood procurement to allow pre-auths for event dates (a short PDF will do)

Alternatively, the provided prepayment link will accept AMEX immediately once the cardholder completes the web auth flow.

Let us know which path you prefer and we’ll expedite.

Regards,
AMEX Support (payments escalation)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, paul.ng@eventlogistics.com, sarah.hartwell@hartwellpharma.com
Date: 2026-10-09T10:45:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Pre-auth declines at Hotel Seaport — need backup plan

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 10:45 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:

Thanks for the updates. Quick status from Finance: we can issue a single-use virtual card for Beacon Events covering room holds and hotel incidentals up to $9,000 total. Virtual card will be delivered via secure link and is restricted to the hotel MID and the event date window.

However, issuing the card requires an approvals packet (short PDF) from org leadership authorizing the spend and the event. Rishi — can you confirm the approval language below so I can attach it and send to AMEX for the whitelist?

Proposed approval language (suggested by Finance):
"Redwood Inference authorizes a single-use virtual card for Beacon Events (Hotel Seaport MID XXXX) to cover room holds and event incidentals for Exec Roundtable on Oct 14–15, 2026. Max authorization $9,000. Card to be delivered to Beacon Events and restricted to the specified merchant and dates."

If Rishi signs off, I’ll generate the virtual card and share the secure link with Paul. That should solve the hotel hold and vendor needs. If we need faster cover for any attendees who already charged personal cards, finance will do an expedited 48-hour reimbursement once receipts are uploaded to Expensify and I have a quick sign-off from Rishi.

Attachments: expense_workaround_template.csv (for any immediate personal-card charges)

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
